title: Reconcile all 28 ADRs and the wayfinder map with the shipped tree
description: Audited every ADR 0001-0028 plus docs/plans/claude-code-first-harness/map.md against executed code, then closed the defects that would break a repository if followed. Six fixes landed on feat/ccodex-rightsizing-controls: the AWS_* env scrub on the muse plane (compliant sweep existed with zero callers); both post-effect-reported-as-clean-refusal exit codes in release_candidate.py; the .agentic-sdlc/rightsize/ namespace collision between ADR-0022 and ADR-0015, reproduced by execution on an already-activated repository; .gitignore for machine-local receipts; and the bundle entry counts the ECC collision argument rests on. Findings left open and needing a decision: the receipt plane disagrees five artifacts to one (ADR-0022 machine-local vs spec ID 11, CONTEXT.md, and issues/09 naming the ccodex XDG plane vs the engine writing target-local); ADR-0005 items 2, 4, and 7 still read as current requirements whose Note disclaims only the split-plane framing, so following item 4 destroys the shipped route; ADR-0003 Confirmation asserts zero gateway hits against 51, and its unrun-canary claim is repeated in launcher code comments; NOTICE owes two third-party donor entries (MADR via adr-lifecycle, CC BY 3.0 via conventional-commits); map.md:58 claims no product choice remains open while the ccodex sdlc profiles surface was silently dropped and version-selection ownership is undetermined; Amendment A's CLAUDE_* allow-by-name half is unimplemented, dropping a privacy flag; four symbols in session-inheritance.sh have no consumer. Exit-code conformance is minority: two of eight surfaces follow Implementation Decision 9.

title: Produce a gate receipt so write-ready can be computed
description: CONTEXT.md:125-128 defines write-ready as a state where portable intent and local receipt agree, custody and trust are admitted, guidance and queue are usable, AND mise run check passes. Implementation Decision 8 forbids the assessor from running a gate itself, so it must read evidence that one passed. scripts/gate_receipt.py has build_receipt, verify_receipt, and verify_toolchain_binding with ZERO producers: nothing in mise.toml, lefthook.yml, or .github/workflows wraps a gate invocation, so the module is exercised only by its own four tests. Slice 4's exit artifact is therefore uncomputable. Add a producer that runs the authoritative gate, captures combined output, and emits a self-hashing receipt bound to argv, exit status, log digest, mise.lock toolchain digest, and cwd. Also close the documented gap at docs/research/2026-08-06-parity-domain-context-research.md:32: status is a bare exit code, so gate-never-ran and gate-ran-and-failed are indistinguishable, and a consumer cannot tell unobserved from failed.

title: Write the tracked repository contract manifest
description: ADR-0022 decision 2 mandates a tracked .agentic-sdlc/repo.toml as the one public file in the private state root. The READER shipped (skills/agentic-sdlc/tools/repository-contract.py, ten-field closed schema) and the activation engine ADMITS the file, but nothing in the repository writes or scaffolds it: repo.toml is referenced only by those two tools, and commands/sdlc-init.md never mentions the file at all. So the runbook ADR-0022 decision 1 governs does not create the artifact decision 2 requires, an operator must hand-author it, and the only statement of the ten required fields is a Python constant. Add a writer that takes every field as an explicit value and refuses to infer any of them. Deliberately NOT detection-based: inferring canonical_guidance or queue_adapter would require the greenfield/brownfield classifier, whose occupied-surface predicates are enumerated in no primary source and which is blocked pending a decision. The writer must produce bytes the reader accepts and the engine admits, must refuse to overwrite an existing manifest without an explicit force, and must not claim readiness, ownership, tool, trust, or route per Implementation Decision 10.

title: Reap the gate child and harden the remaining stderr.buffer writers
description: Two follow-ups surfaced by the gate-receipt review, both PRE-EXISTING rather than introduced by agentic-sdlc-fb9e. First: when an exception escapes _run_gate between subprocess.Popen and proc.wait in scripts/gate_receipt.py, the gate child is never reaped. In-process this surfaces as a timing-dependent ResourceWarning that subprocess N is still running, attributed by tracemalloc; it was observed under the pre-fix code too, which is what establishes it as pre-existing. It changes no exit code and no receipt field, and it cannot fail a test because it fires from __del__. It needs a real decision rather than a reflex fix: reaping in a finally could HANG on a gate that ignores SIGPIPE and keeps writing, which would be worse than leaking a handle, so the choice is between a bounded wait with a kill escalation, a detached reap, and accepting the leak with a named comment. Second, the same text-stream fragility class the review closed in gate_receipt.py still exists unguarded in scripts/release_candidate_acquisition.py at lines 2221, 2226, 3290, and 3322, all of which call sys.stderr.buffer.write directly. A text sys.stderr has no .buffer attribute, and unittest --buffer installs exactly that for every test, so any in-process call of that entrypoint raises AttributeError on the diagnostic path. gate_receipt.py now resolves its sink once through _stderr_mirror and falls back to a decoding write; the same shape would close this. Neither finding blocks anything shipped.

title: Move the activation receipt plane to the ccodex XDG state directory
description: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-17: receipts and recovery journals move to the ccodex XDG state plane, keyed per physical clone or worktree, with an optional repo-local override. This resolves a five-artifact-to-one disagreement in favour of the documents. Spec Implementation Decision 11, CONTEXT.md:109-111, and issues/09:83-88 all name the ccodex XDG state plane; the engine writes target-local .agentic-sdlc/receipts and .agentic-sdlc/transactions. ADR-0022 says only machine-local and names no path, so its own words are satisfied either way. The deciding argument is ADR-0018: sensitive product state lives in its owning plane, and a receipt binds owned paths, hashes, TOOL IDENTITIES and TRUST STATE, which is operator-plane data rather than repository data. Two consequences follow. The .gitignore entries for receipts and transactions become unnecessary, because nothing committable remains, and recovery journals survive a worktree removal instead of dying with the tree. Scope: skills/agentic-sdlc/tools/activation-planner.py and its tests, the .gitignore entries, and correcting AGENTS.md if it describes the old location. Rewrites _validate_private_state, _pin_private, classify_progress_witness, and the recovery classification. An already-activated target carrying target-local receipts needs either an explicit migration path or a named refusal; silently ignoring them would orphan a live activation. Keying must handle a linked worktree and its parent as distinct, per issues/09's separately-keyed requirement. .agentic-sdlc/ retains repo.toml and rightsize/ only.

title: Classify greenfield and brownfield three ways, refusing when ambiguous
description: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-17: implement ADR-0022 decision 4 as a THREE-WAY fail-closed classifier - greenfield, brownfield, or refuse-and-ask - rather than a two-way guess. Brownfield when any named operating-contract surface is occupied. Greenfield ONLY when provably empty: no commits beyond an initial, no guidance file, no queue, no toolchain config. Everything else REFUSES and asks the human. The design constraint is what makes this safe: the occupied-surface predicates are enumerated in no primary source - issues/09:22, ADR-0022:38-39, and to-spec-handoff.md:241-243 all say guidance, queue, decision, toolchain, hook or CI surface without naming a path - and adopting .github/workflows/ as THE CI predicate would classify GitLab, Jenkins, Buildkite, and Woodpecker repositories as greenfield and hand them a full proposed baseline, which is the harm ADR-0022:20-21 rejects by name. Three-way classification makes that specific misclassification impossible, because a repository with no .github but obvious existing content falls into refuse-and-ask rather than into greenfield. An incomplete predicate list then costs a refusal instead of a wrong baseline, which is the correct direction for this repository's fail-closed doctrine. Deliverable is a standalone read-only classifier module plus tests, with commands/sdlc-init.md:70 updated so the runbook stops asking when the answer is derivable and keeps asking when it is not. Do not wire it into the activation engine in this change; a sibling seed is rewriting that file's state plane concurrently.

title: Define baselined as a named-failure subset over gate receipts
description: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-17: baselined means a stored gate receipt carrying the SET of named failing tests, and exact non-worsening means the new run's failure set is a SUBSET of the baseline's. Implementation Decision 17 and issues/09:112-119 require exact non-worsening baselines for remediation-ready, and the term is defined nowhere - a repo-wide search returns prose in CONTEXT.md:131-135, the spec, the tickets, and ADR-0022:43-44 plus two fixture strings, with no implementation. Under Implementation Decision 54's control-strength rule an unenforceable required property makes its feature unsupported, so this definition is what lets remediation-ready ship at all. Subset was chosen over the two cheaper readings deliberately: a status-only or count-based comparison cannot see WHICH tests changed, so a wave that fixes one failure and breaks a different one reads as non-worsening, which is exactly what the word exact in ID 17 exists to prevent. Buildable now that agentic-sdlc-fb9e shipped the producer. Needs the receipt to record failure identities alongside status and log_digest as an additive digest-covered field, so pre-existing receipts must keep verifying, and a comparison that reports the newly-failing set by name rather than a boolean. Scope: scripts/gate_receipt.py and its tests plus the comparison. Do NOT change where a receipt is written; a sibling seed is moving that plane concurrently, so keep the destination a caller-supplied argument.

title: Stop apply_command defaulting effect none for a post-publication refusal
description: SIXTH instance in this project of one defect class: something became true and the code reported that nothing had. Found by the agentic-sdlc-7ebc implementer while re-reading its own diff against exactly that question, PRE-EXISTING rather than introduced, and correctly left unfixed because it belongs to apply_command rather than to that ticket's scope. _validate_private_state is reachable AFTER publication through write_commit, capture_git_observation, validate_internal_status_records. apply_command's except handler defaults effect to none for ANY refusal regardless of where it was raised, so a refusal raised post-publication reports status refused with effect none while the product is on disk. Measured on unmodified code: control with no injection gives 0 committed effect committed published True; with repo-local state injected it gives 3 refused effect none published True. Per Implementation Decision 9 a refusal after a durable effect is 4, an admitted partial or unknown effect, never 3 with effect none. Reachable only through concurrent external mutation of managed paths during a write command, which AGENTS.md declares unsupported, so severity is bounded -- but the handler's shape is the defect, not the trigger. The 7ebc change deliberately did NOT widen it: the probe took an admission flag and the single post-publish caller passes admission false, while every genuine admission surface still validates before any effect and classify_progress_witness keeps the probe because it converts every error to effect_unknown rather than a clean claim. The fix is to derive the reported effect from what was actually admitted, the way scripts/release_candidate.py and scripts/gate_receipt.py now both do through a single escalation choke point, rather than defaulting it per raise site.

title: Assemble the write-ready / remediation-ready / refused activation result
description: Slice 4 exit artifact (map build-sequence step 4; ADR-0022 decision 7; to-spec-handoff.md:255-259). Compose the four landed operands - repository-classifier three-way verdict, repository-contract-writer manifest, activation-planner receipt/effects, gate_baseline named-failure subset - into exactly one terminal state: write-ready (full portable and local contract admitted; normal waves may write), remediation-ready (exact known gate failures baselined, no ownership/trust/credential/path blocker; only named hygiene waves may write; never claims the gate passes), or refused/partial/unknown-effect with exact recovery evidence. One full greenfield and one brownfield assessed journey must drive it.

title: WSL2 backwards clock steps intermittently redden the journal monotonicity check
description: Found while verifying agentic-sdlc-42ed. A 100-second CLOCK_REALTIME monitor observed four backwards steps of 0.22-0.53s (WSL2 time sync). Any two journal appends straddling a step across a second boundary make the recorded_at chain non-monotonic, so validate_bundle.py operation_journal ordering check fails test_fault_after_each_durable_phase_returns_four_and_preserves_exact_journal (phases pinned/receipted) intermittently: 1 failure observed, then 0 in 60 repeats + 14 suite runs. Will bite mise run check intermittently on this host. Not a code defect; decide whether the check should tolerate bounded regression or the journal should use a monotonic source.

title: Effect-ledger follow-ups from the b6cb adversarial verification
description: Non-blocking findings from the agentic-sdlc-b6cb verifier, all confirmed: (1) dead code - _restore_exchange_mismatch and the Path-form _renameat2 have zero callers, write_progress unpinned fallback via _replace_metadata is unreachable; delete rather than test. (2) _effect_ledger replaces rather than nests, so an inner command invocation would hide its effects from an outer report; no handler calls another today - fix the docstring or make it nest. (3) _mkdir_at fchmod 0700 on an already-present directory is an unadmitted mutation. (4) no ledger injection sweep covers the recover verbs (verified by hand only). (5) admitted_effects on a no-op apply prints the plane absolute path (operator home) into result JSON while reasons deliberately redact plane paths - inconsistent, untested. (6) two sweep-test docstrings overclaim (any-admit-deletion-changes-list; whole-program sweep).

title: Stamp baseline identity into the gate-baseline comparison and bind it at derivation
description: Fable-lane finding from the agentic-sdlc-6b0d verification (non-blocking, unclosable inside activation-result.py): gate-baseline-comparison/v1 carries no baseline identity - no baseline cwd, no baseline receipt self_digest - so a comparison computed against another repository baseline receipt, or a fully hand-written comparison naming no receipts at all, reaches remediation-ready. Candidate-side value binding (gate label + candidate_failing set + candidate_outcome) is sound and needs no digest. Fix shape: gate_baseline.py compare stamps baseline cwd and baseline receipt self_digest into the report; activation-result.py then requires the stamped baseline cwd to agree with the target and surfaces the digest in evidence. Cross-file change, own mutation tests both sides.

title: Terminal-state derivation cannot prove artifact freshness; bind head or time linkage in slice 6
description: Second Fable-lane finding from agentic-sdlc-6b0d: a stale matched plan+apply pair from an earlier cleaner tree plus a fresh passing gate receipt derives write-ready, because no operand artifact carries head or time linkage that a read-only composer could check (receipt and activation result have no common anchor). Documented as a named residual in activation-result.py. The durable closure belongs to slice 6 planning/observability: PlanningSnapshot / immutable receipt families should bind repository head identity so the composer can refuse a pair that predates the current tree. Decide there whether the binding is head sha, receipt chain, or monotonic operation ids.

title: Reconcile ADR-0005, ADR-0003, NOTICE, and the map with the operator decisions
description: Four operator decisions from the agentic-sdlc-5d58 audit, 2026-08-18, all docs-plane: (1) extend ADR-0005 Status Note to name decision items 2, 4, and 7 as superseded by ADR-0014 item by item (entry point moved to ccodex; the subscription-OAuth prohibition is gone - sk-ant-oat* accepted; claude-subscription route removed). (2) rewrite ADR-0003 Confirmation to the post-ADR-0014 reality (the zero-gateway-hits rg pin is false at ~51 hits; the preserved property is that a gateway is described but never a required install or gate component) and repoint the opencodex-claude.sh comment asserting the canary is still unrun toward where canary status is recorded rather than a prose fact. (3) add the two NOTICE donor entries ADR-0001 requires: MADR via the adr-lifecycle reference, Conventional Commits under CC BY 3.0. (4) correct map.md:58 to name the two open product choices instead of claiming none remain.

title: Implement Amendment A allow-by-name so named CLAUDE_* flags survive the scrub
description: Operator decision 2026-08-18: implement ADR-0010 Amendment A allow-by-name half. The scrub currently sweeps every CLAUDE_* variable, dropping CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC (a privacy flag). Wire or replace the four orphaned session-inheritance.sh symbols (scrub_and_restore_claude_env, CLAUDE_INHERITED_ENV_VARS, CLAUDE_DENIED_ENV_VARS, report_env_policy) into one shared helper both planes use; muse-claude.sh scrub_anthropic_env keeps its denials (AWS prefix, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED, FALLBACK_FOR_ALL_PRIMARY_MODELS, API_TIMEOUT_MS) while allowing the named list. Credential-adjacent: failure mode is allowing too much across the boundary, so the review is Fable-lane and every allowed name needs a stated reason.

title: Converge the six nonconforming command surfaces to Implementation Decision 9
description: Operator decision 2026-08-18: converge rather than re-scope. Implementation Decision 9 (0 success/no-effect, 1 internal pre-effect, 2 grammar/schema, 3 clean refusal pre-effect, 4 admitted partial-or-unknown) is followed by two of eight command surfaces (the gate/activation family). Umbrella: enumerate the six nonconforming surfaces exactly, then queue one child seed per surface applying the class-closure discipline the gate family got - reproduce, enumerate every exit, single derivation point, mutation tests in both directions.

title: Decide: restore or formally drop the ccodex sdlc profiles surface
description: DECIDED 2026-08-20 by the operator: formally dropped. Each first-party profile keeps its own receipt-backed front door (ccodex routes for routed models, the AutoEnvelope admission chain for bounded recursion, the libraries tasks for companions) and ccodex sdlc status reports active profiles read-only without owning their mutation. Rationale: one capability, one front door; a generic profiles verb would duplicate authority over state that already has exactly one receipt-backed mutation path. Reversible later only as a new decision. Original context: the surface was silently dropped from the plan and the map audit turned that into this decision ticket.

title: Decide: who owns release version selection at install time
description: DECIDED 2026-08-20 by the operator: the operator owns release version selection, expressed through mise's native pin (explicit version or unpinned meaning latest stable release). The release manifest owns compatibility claims only, per ADR-0027's capability-evidence admission; the ccodex sdlc install lifecycle owns verification only — it records the exact resolved version into the ownership receipt and refuses a declared incompatibility rather than substituting a version silently. Consistent with map.md's delegation of version acquisition and selection to mise and with the no-self-updater non-goal. Original context: ownership was undetermined among installer lifecycle, release manifest, and operator.

title: Unprefixed credential names reach the launched child verbatim (MODEL_API_KEY)
description: Found by the Fable-lane credential-boundary review of agentic-sdlc-71f4 and reproduced identically against HEAD, so it is pre-existing rather than a regression: the environment scrub denies ANTHROPIC_*/CLAUDE_*/AWS_* by prefix plus three named unprefixed hazards (NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED, FALLBACK_FOR_ALL_PRIMARY_MODELS, API_TIMEOUT_MS), so an unprefixed credential name is not swept. Measured: MODEL_API_KEY reaches the child verbatim alongside ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN carrying the same value. Decide whether the deny policy gains an unprefixed credential-name class (and how it stays maintainable without becoming a value scanner - ADR-0010 Amendment A deliberately makes this a NAME policy), or whether the limit is documented and accepted. Related documented limit from the same review: a secret an operator sets under an allowed name crosses as that variable value.

title: Record every wave node disposition in an append-only wave journal
description: Slice 5 substrate (issue 07 State/continuation + Completion conditions 1 and 7). One read/append tool owning the wave journal: each node records inputs, outputs, RuntimeAssignment, timestamps, result, and evidence, and every required node reaches exactly one of admitted success, approved skip, or explicit blocked disposition. Also records budgets, retries, plan revisions, and approvals so condition 7 traceability is derivable rather than asserted. Append-only with effect admission at the instant a record becomes durable (the effect-admission class rule); a partial append is exit 4, never a clean refusal. Deterministic canonical JSON, schema-tagged.

title: Admit or refuse a RuntimeAssignment before spawn and detect unexplained substitution
description: Slice 5 dispatch admission (issue 07 Roles/authority/routing + Completion condition 2; AGENTS.md RuntimeAssignment rules). Read-only admission tool: resolution_state must be resolved, exact model and effort request injection is mandatory and immutable, requested tier and resolved provider/model stay separate facts, resolved is recorded only after adapter readback, and requested/inherited/unresolved/incomplete stops before dispatch and therefore before spawn with a named refusal plus a SeedProposal shape. Separately: given a receipt, decide whether the served provider/model matches what was requested and classify any difference as explained substitution or UNEXPLAINED (which blocks wave completion). Effective effort/context readback may be honestly unavailable and requested values never become readback.

title: Derive the terminal wave verdict: accepted, remediation-progress, or blocked
description: Slice 5 EXIT ARTIFACT (map build-sequence step 5; product spec 597-603; issue 07 Completion and adversarial review). Compose the wave journal, RuntimeAssignment admissions, workstream review verdicts, fan-in authorization, the gate receipt and baseline comparison, and the critic findings into exactly one terminal state: accepted (normal delivery wave, authoritative repository gate passes, all eight completion conditions met), remediation-progress (focused gates pass AND the exact global failure baseline does not worsen; never claims gate-passing or write-ready), or blocked. Fail-closed and read-only like activation-result.py: any unmet condition is a named refusal, ambiguity is blocked rather than guessed, no input combination yields two states or none. The conductor owns classification: a finding classified blocking (acceptance-criteria violation, safety regression, corrupted evidence, failed authoritative gate) prevents completion; non-blocking findings become Seeds and a wave may complete with them. Workflow-process completion alone is never a product-success verdict.

title: Decide whether pstack can be onboarded, given it has no Claude Code front door
description: DECIDED 2026-08-20 by the operator: pstack IS onboardable, through a custom onboarding route rather than a simple front-door install — it is on par with mattpocock/skills in capability terms and can level up the agentic-sdlc ecosystem. The route: execute the shipped porting recipe (skills/external-skill-libraries/references/porting-a-foreign-plugin.md) against pristine upstream HEAD with a recorded commit pin; the ported plugin lands in the operator's home under the operator's ownership; upstream bytes never enter this repository; re-porting on upstream updates is a recipe re-run. This creates a second catalog class (ported libraries) beside ADR-0009's front-door libraries; the doctrine recording and skill-surface documentation are queued as their own implementation seed.

title: Gather pstack upstream evidence from pristine HEAD, never the ported working tree
description: CLOSED 2026-08-20: the practice this seed demanded — gather pstack upstream evidence from pristine HEAD, never the ported working tree — is encoded in the shipped porting recipe (checklist item on never citing a ported tree for upstream claims) and was applied by the recipe's own adversarial verification. title: pass-budget charge is not idempotent: a retry double-charges the ledger

Note the charge-then-check ordering at pass-budget.py:103 is DELIBERATE and correct - it exists so a crash cannot hand out free passes - so the fix is an idempotency key (attempt or operation id) that makes a repeated charge for the same attempt converge rather than accumulate, per the make-operations-idempotent discipline. The exit-code conformance work is the same ticket: a charge whose durable increment landed must not report a clean pre-effect refusal. Enumeration also corrected the umbrella premise: there are 24 CLI surfaces, not 8, of which 9 conform, 6 are read-only and effect-incapable so 3 and 4 are legitimately unreachable, and 8 are nonconforming; the prior 2-of-8 figure was an undercount.
